QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_39

question.text: A distribution of AIF annual returns with skewness = -2.22 suggests:

answer.text: Large negative outliers below the mean, indicating elevated downside risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Skewness below zero indicates a negatively skewed distribution with a long left tail and large negative outliers below the mean, pointing to higher downside risk. The Trap: Option A describes positive skewness (>0). Option B describes a symmetrical distribution with skew = 0. Option C confuses skewness with kurtosis. Note: The negative-skew interpretation is taken from the risk-measure section of the workbook.
